keyVerseText: When they took hold of thee by thy hand, thou didst break, and rend all their shoulder: and when they leaned upon thee, thou brakest, and madest all their loins to be at a stand.
rootMeaning: The root of עָמַד (ʻâmad) is מָעַד (mâʻad), which carries the fundamental idea of causing to shake, slip, or totter. This root conveys not only the physical act of standing but also the dynamic tension between stability and instability. Thus, the literal sense of ʻâmad goes beyond merely 'standing' to include the concept of remaining firm or causing something else to be unsteady or brought to a halt.
usageInScripture: The word עָמַד (ʻâmad) appears with the meaning 'to be at a stand' in Scripture, emphasizing a state of standing firm or remaining in place. Although its occurrences are limited, the consistent translation reveals its core semantic range centered on standing, enduring, or causing to stand. This usage highlights both physical and metaphorical senses of stability and endurance, reflecting the tension between steadfastness and shaking inherent in its root.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding עָמַד (ʻâmad) enriches our grasp of biblical themes of endurance and divine strength. The word's root meaning of causing to shake or totter reminds us of human frailty and the instability of relying on earthly strength. In contrast, ʻâmad's sense of standing firm points to God's sustaining power that enables His people to endure trials without falling. This duality underscores the Christian faith's call to trust in Christ, who steadies us amid life's uncertainties and makes us able to stand unshaken.
keyVerseReflection: In Ezekiel 29:7, the phrase 'thou brakest, and madest all their loins to be at a stand' uses עָמַד to depict a powerful act of divine judgment that causes enemies to be immobilized or rendered ineffective. Here, the word conveys not just physical standing but a forced cessation—an enforced stability that results from God's sovereign intervention. This highlights God's authority to both shake and establish, reinforcing His control over the fate of nations and His people.
